BULK-PAGE-TITLE

BULK-MOVABLE-HEADING

BULK-MOVABLE-ONE. The paragraph is long on purpose: a chunk budget is counted in characters, and a subtree that fits inside its parent's chunk never exercises the gate this fixture exists to reach. Bound periodicals, manuscripts and plate volumes transferred from the reading room.

BULK-MOVABLE-TWO. A second paragraph of comparable weight, so that the block stays over the budget even when the harness lowers it. Holdings notes, shelfmarks, and the accession registers that go with them.

BULK-MOVABLE-THREE. And a third, because the point is not to be near the boundary but comfortably past it, in every configuration the axes allow.

BULK-ANCHORED-HEADING

BULK-ANCHORED-ONE. This block never moves. It is here so that the default slot is not left empty by the reassignment, which would make the slot change shape as well as contents and confuse what is being measured.

BULK-ANCHORED-TWO. More of the same, at the same weight, for the same reason: the two blocks have to be comparable or the comparison says nothing about the gate.
